summary:
FieldShift is an agricultural intelligence platform designed to help understand field conditions and support more informed crop-management decisions using real Earth observation and environmental data.

The project focuses initially on Story County, Iowa, USA, using a region-specific implementation while keeping the architecture suitable for expansion to other regions.

FieldShift brings together agricultural and environmental information, including NASA data and USDA datasets, through a data-processing pipeline. The goal is to transform raw observations into understandable indicators related to soil conditions, crop history, weather patterns and agricultural risks.

The platform aims to make complex scientific datasets easier to interpret through an interactive interface and evidence-based analysis. Its recommendations are intended to be explainable, with data sources, limitations and uncertainty made visible rather than presenting unsupported predictions as facts.
details:
Problem

Agricultural decisions depend on several interconnected factors, including soil characteristics, historical crop patterns, weather conditions, vegetation health and environmental risks. However, this information is often distributed across different scientific and agricultural data sources, making it difficult to interpret and use together.

FieldShift aims to make these datasets more accessible and useful for agricultural analysis.

Our Solution

FieldShift is an agricultural intelligence platform that combines Earth observation, environmental and agricultural datasets to help users understand regional and field-level agricultural conditions.

For the initial implementation, we focus on Story County, Iowa, USA. This limited geographical scope allows us to build and demonstrate a real-data pipeline instead of presenting simulated results or unsupported global coverage.

The platform is designed around the following capabilities:

  • Agricultural land and crop-history analysis.
  • Soil-property analysis using authoritative soil datasets.
  • Weather and climate information.
  • Satellite-based vegetation monitoring.
  • Environmental and agricultural risk indicators.
  • Explainable crop-rotation analysis and recommendations.

Only indicators supported by the available datasets and implemented calculations will be presented as operational features.

Data Sources

NASA data is used as part of the environmental data pipeline. Additional agricultural and geospatial information is obtained from USDA and other relevant public sources.

The pipeline retrieves source data, preserves the original observations, processes the information and makes the resulting data available to the application.

Technology

The project uses:

  • Python and FastAPI for backend services and data processing.
  • React and TypeScript for the frontend.
  • MapLibre GL JS for geographical visualization.
  • NASA and USDA data services for real-world observations and agricultural information.
  • Data-processing and analysis methods to derive understandable agricultural indicators.

Artificial Intelligence

AI-assisted development tools and coding agents are used to accelerate implementation, assist with debugging, and support development and documentation.

Any AI-generated code or data-related content is identified appropriately. Agricultural indicators and recommendations are intended to be grounded in actual source data and documented calculations rather than fabricated outputs.

Expected Impact

FieldShift aims to make complex Earth observation and agricultural datasets easier to understand and use. By connecting environmental information with agricultural analysis, the platform can help users identify relevant conditions, understand potential risks and make better-informed decisions.

The initial demonstration focuses on a limited geographical region, with the possibility of expanding the data pipeline to additional regions in future development.
